file_name: 2025 - The Risk and the Reward An In-depth Evaluation of Strategic Aggressiveness in Men s Tennis - Venkatesh et al.pdf
universal_lens: Strategic aggressiveness in tennis as a stochastic control problem with state-dependent reward functions and dynamic decision thresholds. A Bayesian risk-reward optimization framework integrating player ranking, situational aggressiveness, and reward expectation across serve, return, and rally contexts.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of optimal aggressiveness levels using conformal predictive distributions over shot-by-shot outcomes, conditioned on match state and player rank. GSI employs conformal predictive inference to map player aggressiveness levels to expected reward distributions using XGBoost regression models with RMSE thresholds.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine models tactical aggression as a Markov decision process with state transitions governed by shot outcomes and environmental constraints. GSE applies Markovian state transitions to model tactical shifts in aggressiveness based on score and rank differentials, enabling dynamic decision-making in real-time rallies.
